module_microarchitecture.name: sram_mbist_demo_controller
module_microarchitecture.implementation_style: Single-clock controller with a minimal register-map front end and a single SRAM functional access path through child instance u_sram.
module_microarchitecture.control_strategy: Decode wr_en/wr_addr/wr_data for register writes and rd_en/rd_addr for readback. Use a straightforward write/read request flow for MEM_ADDR, MEM_WDATA, MEM_CONTROL, and BIST_CONTROL, with CONTROL bits gating operation and IRQ enable. BIST_start is treated as an explicit request source alongside software START.
module_microarchitecture.state_strategy: Use small registered state for CONTROL, STATUS, MEM_ADDR, MEM_WDATA, MEM_RDATA, MEM_CONTROL, BIST_CONTROL, BIST_STATUS, IRQ_STATUS, a simple busy indicator, and latched BIST completion/failure bookkeeping including last_fail_addr. Reset clears all visible state and deselects the memory path.
module_microarchitecture.output_strategy: Drive rd_data from the selected register or memory readback value, ready from controller idle/operational state, bist_done and bist_fail from latched BIST status, and irq from IRQ_ENABLE combined with latched IRQ status.
ownership_notes: Controller owns rd_data, ready, bist_done, bist_fail, irq, and the SRAM sideband signals sram_csb, sram_web, sram_addr, and sram_din.
Controller observes sram_dout from the child wrapper and captures it into MEM_RDATA/readback state.
No hidden interface is introduced; the controller remains the top and the wrapper stays a child instance named u_sram.

module_microarchitecture.name: demo_sram_32x256_wrapper
module_microarchitecture.implementation_style: Macro-compatible functional SRAM wrapper with an identical interface whether bound to prebuilt Sky130 collateral or to the synthesizable fallback model.
module_microarchitecture.control_strategy: Pass the controller's single functional access path through clk, csb, web, addr, din, and dout. Keep the interface stable so tools can recognize SRAM intent and MBIST insertion points.
module_microarchitecture.state_strategy: No architectural state is required in the wrapper description; it simply binds the active implementation and preserves the memory contract.
module_microarchitecture.output_strategy: Forward memory read data on dout from either the Sky130 macro binding or the fallback model binding without changing the port list.
ownership_notes: clk, csb, web, addr, and din are wrapper inputs and must not be driven by the wrapper.
If a second read port exists in the underlying macro, it is not used by the controller and may be tied off or reserved within the binding layer without changing this wrapper interface.

module_microarchitecture.name: demo_sram_32x256_model
module_microarchitecture.implementation_style: Synthesizable 256x32 synchronous memory fallback that mirrors the wrapper interface exactly.
module_microarchitecture.control_strategy: Implement basic synchronous read/write behavior behind the same clk/csb/web/addr/din/dout contract so simulation and synthesis remain straightforward when prebuilt macro collateral is unavailable.
module_microarchitecture.state_strategy: Use a simple 256-entry storage array with registered access behavior; no vendor primitives or complex control are implied.
module_microarchitecture.output_strategy: Return the selected word on dout according to the functional memory contract, enabling the controller to read back data through the same path as the macro binding.
ownership_notes: clk, csb, web, addr, and din are model inputs.
The fallback model is implementation collateral only and does not alter the controller interface or hierarchy.

fsm_intent.description: No complex FSM is implied. The controller can be implemented as a small set of register-update and memory-access sequencing rules with a simple busy/idle indication, rather than a multi-state controller. BIST request/status behavior is described through latched control and status bits, not a detailed explicit state machine.

internal_storage: busy or equivalent simple internal activity flag
output_mapping: rd_data reflects the addressed register readback or MEM_RDATA as selected by rd_addr.
bist_done reflects latched BIST completion status.
bist_fail reflects latched BIST failure status.
irq asserts only when IRQ_ENABLE is set and a latched BIST done/fail event is present.

sequencing_notes: Reset places the controller in a safe deselected state, clears all visible registers and latched status, and clears software-visible read data.
Writes to CONTROL, MEM_ADDR, MEM_WDATA, MEM_CONTROL, BIST_CONTROL, and IRQ_CLEAR update the corresponding internal registers using the specified bit fields only.
MEM_CONTROL.MEM_WRITE and MEM_CONTROL.MEM_READ are simple request bits that drive the wrapper access path one operation at a time.
BIST_CONTROL.START and the external bist_start input both act as request sources for BIST initiation; BIST_CONTROL.CLEAR_RESULT clears latched BIST result state.
IRQ_STATUS is latched until cleared by IRQ_CLEAR using write-one-to-clear behavior.

ready may be held as a simple indication of controller availability and deasserted only when a memory/BIST operation is actively being serviced, keeping the implementation simple for fast integration.
timing_notes: Memory wrapper/model interface is synchronous and intentionally simple for synthesis and MBIST detection.
No multi-cycle protocol or vendor-specific timing behavior is implied beyond basic registered memory access.
The design should preserve macro detectability by keeping the child memory instance u_sram and the canonical SRAM port naming intact.
consistency_notes: No hierarchy, ports, or filenames may differ from digital_spec_json.
